skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI video workflows through the inference.sh CLI, including text-to-video, image-to-video, avatars, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and clip merging.
skill.summary: Create and refine AI videos with inference.sh models from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are Markdown formatting, example commands, placeholder URLs, and documentation links rather than Ruby backtick execution or hidden callbacks. I added semantic findings for shell quoting risk in command examples and for remote processing privacy disclosure. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious command intent.

remediation.issue: CLI examples embed request data inside shell arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Show safer input handling, such as reading request data from a file or requiring proper shell escaping for user text.
Add a clear note that prompts and media URLs are sent to inference.sh and selected model providers.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Quoting Risk in CLI Examples
semantic_findings.description: Several examples pass request data directly in shell arguments. If an assistant inserts a user prompt or URL containing a single quote without escaping, the shell could parse unintended tokens before belt receives the request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples show shell-quoted request bodies, and the skill is intended to adapt them to user prompts. The risk depends on future interpolation behavior, so confidence is medium.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Media Processing Requires Privacy Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The skill sends prompts and user media URLs to inference.sh video apps for generation, avatar, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and merging. This is the advertised feature, but users need a privacy warning before using sensitive media.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill clearly documents remote CLI use and URL-based media inputs. I found no covert exfiltration, so severity stays low.

content.value_statement: Producing short videos across many AI models requires model-specific commands and input formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs inference.sh belt commands for supported video generation workflows.
Lists video model IDs for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, and utility tasks.
Provides examples for Google Veo, Grok Video, Wan, Seedance, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, and utility apps.
Supports video enhancement tasks such as upscaling, foley generation, and clip merging.
Points users to related skills for narration, image generation, and social posting workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account.
Generation speed, cost, and quality depend on the selected model provider.
Prompts and media URLs are processed by remote services, so sensitive assets need review.
Does not guarantee that every listed model remains available.

use_cases.title: Draft Marketing Clips
use_cases.description: Create short campaign videos from product ideas, launch messages, or social concepts.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Images
use_cases.description: Turn approved product or scene images into motion clips for demos and presentations.

use_cases.title: Build Avatar Videos
use_cases.description: Combine portrait images and narration audio into talking-head or lipsync videos.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a First Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short AI video for [topic]. Use a fast model and suggest the prompt, duration, and output settings before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [image URL] into a moving clip. Describe the motion, camera movement, and model choice before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [portrait URL] and [audio URL] to make a talking avatar. Choose a suitable model and explain privacy concerns first.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and run a workflow that creates source clips, adds foley, upscales the final video, and prepares sharing notes.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second nature video for a social post.
output_examples.output: Selected a fast Veo model, prepared a concise cinematic prompt, and ran the generation through inference.sh.

output_examples.input: Animate a product photo with a slow camera move.
output_examples.output: Recommended an image-to-video model, described the motion plan, and used the supplied image URL as the source.

output_examples.input: Make a talking avatar from a portrait and narration track.
output_examples.output: Checked the remote media links, selected an avatar model, and warned that the portrait and audio are processed remotely.

best_practices: Use approved media URLs and avoid sensitive personal assets unless remote processing is permitted.
Start with fast models for drafts, then rerun final prompts on higher quality models.
Specify subject, camera motion, duration, style, and audio needs in each prompt.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private portraits, voices, or unreleased product media without approval.
Do not use vague prompts that omit subject, motion, duration, or style.
Do not assume model availability, pricing, or output rights without checking current provider terms.

faq.question: Does this skill create videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI to run remote model apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it animate an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples for Wan, Seedance, and related models.

faq.question: Can it create talking avatars?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse lipsync workflows.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need the inference.sh CLI, called belt, and a logged-in account.

faq.question: Should sensitive media be used?
faq.answer: Only when remote processing is approved. Prompts and media URLs may be sent to model providers.
